The model is a brilliant mind that has read almost everything and knows nothing about you. The whole world is stuck at chat level. Learning AI for real starts when you give that mind YOUR world: plain files about what you sell, who your customers are, how you talk. That's context. Same model everyone uses — yours knows your customers by name. PART 2 — AUTOMATIONS. Work that fires on its own when something happens. Invoice lands → logged → answered, nobody touched anything. And once you can do that, you can describe a tool you wish existed and build it: your ideas turn into products. PART 3 — AI EMPLOYEES. An agent is AI with hands and a goal: plan, do, check, fix, again — until the job is done. An AI employee is an agent that STAYS: memory so corrections stick, skills written once and followed every time, working inside your real accounts, behind guardrails — keys only to its own work, and the risky moves wait for your yes. I run my whole business this way. They work while I sleep; mornings, the finished work is waiting. THREE DOORS for the skills: your own work (hand off the repeating hours), your ideas (products people use), or clients (companies pay real money for people who can wire AI into an operation). None of this needs code. First time in history you build all of it in plain English. The ramp: TODAY write your context files → THIS WEEK first automation → THIS MONTH first agent → THEN your first employee. Each step makes the next one easy. A mind alone is potential. Four ways I use AI to make money There are four different places AI skills can create value. The right starting point depends on the work you already understand. 1. Inside your job. Build a knowledge base from information you are allowed to use, connect relevant tools, and document repeatable procedures. Useful reports and clearer answers make the value visible to your team. 2. Consulting. Map how work actually moves before choosing a tool. Find the bottleneck, then fix it with automation, AI, or a simpler process. The finished improvement is what a client pays for. 3. Production services. Package a finished image, video, or other creative deliverable around the client's need. Price the complete work, including your judgment, revisions, and delivery. 4. Your own product. Build a useful tool, course, template, or digital resource that more than one customer can buy. It takes work to create, market, support, and improve it, but you can reuse the product rather than starting each delivery from scratch. If you already have a job, start with a useful internal task. If you run a business, improve a process you know first. That experience makes it easier to show someone else what you can deliver. #aiautomation #aiagent #aiemployee

The model isn’t the agent. An LLM can decide what should happen next—but it can’t actually search the web, run code, call an API, or complete a task by itself. That’s where the AI harness comes in. It gives the model tools, executes its actions, tracks context, handles errors, and feeds the results back so the model can decide what to do next. LLM = the brain.  Harness = what turns the brain into an agent. Once you understand harnesses, modern AI agents make a lot more sense. #AI #ArtificialIntelligence #AIAgents #LLM #MachineLearning
